chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa and Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'The people of Mecca complete the prayer at Arafat.' He said, 'Woe to them or woe to them! And which journey is harder than it? No, they do not complete it.'
And Umrah is an obligation like Hajj; it is not permissible to leave it in any case. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: Do pilgrims shorten their prayer at Arafat during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the prevailing practice in Mecca of shortening the prayer to three rak'ahs at Arafat, arguing that the spiritual intensity of the Hajj journey necessitates the full four-rak'ah prayer. He further establishes the independent obligatory status of Umrah, asserting it is a mandatory duty equal to Hajj that cannot be omitted under any circumstances. This narration highlights the scholarly debate between the people of Mecca and the Ahl al-Bayt regarding ritual precision during the sacred months.
